# Spring Boot

> Javaアプリケーション開発者向けに、組み込みサーバー・自動設定・AOT処理などを備えたSpring Bootフレームワークを提供し、設定不要で本番稼働可能なスタンドアロンアプリを構築できる。

## Guide

- [All Modules](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/dokka/dokka-overview.md): _See also the <a href="../java/index.html" target="_blank">Java API documentation (Javadoc)</a>._
- [Ahead-of-Time Processing](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/aot.adoc): Spring AOT is a process that analyzes your code at build-time in order to generate an optimized version of it.
- [Getting Started](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/getting-started.adoc): To get started with the plugin it needs to be applied to your project.
- [Gradle Plugin](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/index.adoc): The Spring Boot Gradle Plugin provides Spring Boot support in Gradle.
- [Integrating with Actuator](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/integrating-with-actuator.adoc): Spring Boot Actuator's info endpoint automatically publishes information about your build in the presence of a META-INF/build-info.properties file.
- [Introduction](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/introduction.adoc): The Spring Boot Gradle Plugin provides Spring Boot support in Gradle.
- [Managing Dependencies](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/managing-dependencies.adoc): To manage dependencies in your Spring Boot application, you can either apply the {url-dependency-management-plugin-site}[io.spring.dependency-management] plugin or use Gradle's native bom support.
- [Packaging OCI Images](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/packaging-oci-image.adoc): The plugin can create an OCI image from a jar or war file using Cloud Native Buildpacks (CNB).
- [Packaging Executable Archives](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/packaging.adoc): The plugin can create executable archives (jar files and war files) that contain all of an application's dependencies and can then be run with java -jar.
- [Publishing your Application](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/publishing.adoc): To publish your Spring Boot jar or war, add it to the publication using the artifact method on MavenPublication.
- [Reacting to Other Plugins](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/reacting.adoc): When another plugin is applied the Spring Boot plugin reacts by making various changes to the project's configuration.
- [Running your Application with Gradle](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/pages/running.adoc): To run your application without first building an archive use the bootRun task:
- [Nav Gradle Plugin](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-gradle-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/gradle-plugin/partials/nav-gradle-plugin.adoc)
- [Ahead-of-Time Processing](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/aot.adoc): Spring AOT is a process that analyzes your application at build-time and generate an optimized version of it.
- [Packaging OCI Images](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/build-image.adoc): The plugin can create an OCI image from a jar or war file using Cloud Native Buildpacks (CNB).
- [Integrating with Actuator](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/build-info.adoc): Spring Boot Actuator displays build-related information if a META-INF/build-info.properties file is present.
- [Getting Started](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/getting-started.adoc): To use the Spring Boot Maven Plugin, include the appropriate XML in the plugins section of your pom.xml, as shown in the following example:
- [Goals](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/goals.adoc): The Spring Boot Plugin has the following goals:
- [Help Information](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/help.adoc): The help goal is a standard goal that  displays information on the capabilities of the plugin.
- [Maven Plugin](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/index.adoc): The Spring Boot Maven Plugin provides Spring Boot support in Apache Maven.
- [Running Integration Tests](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/integration-tests.adoc): While you may start your Spring Boot application very easily from your test (or test suite) itself, it may be desirable to handle that in the build itself.
- [Packaging Executable Archives](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/packaging.adoc): The plugin can create executable archives (jar files and war files) that contain all of an application's dependencies and can then be run with java -jar.
- [Running your Application with Maven](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/run.adoc): The plugin includes a run goal which can be used to launch your application from the command line, as shown in the following example:
- [Using the Plugin](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/pages/using.adoc): Maven users can inherit from the spring-boot-starter-parent project to obtain sensible defaults.
- [Nav Maven Plugin](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/build-plugin/spring-boot-maven-plugin/src/docs/antora/modules/maven-plugin/partials/nav-maven-plugin.adoc)
- [Audit Events (`auditevents`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/auditevents.adoc): The auditevents endpoint provides information about the application's audit events.
- [Beans (`beans`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/beans.adoc): The beans endpoint provides information about the application's beans.
- [Caches (`caches`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/caches.adoc): The caches endpoint provides access to the application's caches.
- [Conditions Evaluation Report (`conditions`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/conditions.adoc): The conditions endpoint provides information about the evaluation of conditions on configuration and auto-configuration classes.
- [Configuration Properties (`configprops`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/configprops.adoc): The configprops endpoint provides information about the application's @ConfigurationProperties beans.
- [Environment (`env`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/env.adoc): The env endpoint provides information about the application's Environment.
- [Flyway (`flyway`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/flyway.adoc): The flyway endpoint provides information about database migrations performed by Flyway.
- [Health (`health`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/health.adoc): The health endpoint provides detailed information about the health of the application.
- [Heap Dump (`heapdump`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/heapdump.adoc): The heapdump endpoint provides a heap dump from the application's JVM.
- [HTTP Exchanges (`httpexchanges`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/httpexchanges.adoc): The httpexchanges endpoint provides information about HTTP request-response exchanges.
- [Actuator REST API](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/index.adoc): This API documentation describes Spring Boot Actuators web endpoints.
- [Info (`info`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/info.adoc): The info endpoint provides general information about the application.
- [Spring Integration Graph (`integrationgraph`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/integrationgraph.adoc): The integrationgraph endpoint exposes a graph containing all Spring Integration components.
- [Liquibase (`liquibase`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/liquibase.adoc): The liquibase endpoint provides information about database change sets applied by Liquibase.
- [Log File (`logfile`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/logfile.adoc): The logfile endpoint provides access to the contents of the application's log file.
- [Loggers (`loggers`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/loggers.adoc): The loggers endpoint provides access to the application's loggers and the configuration of their levels.
- [Mappings (`mappings`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/mappings.adoc): The mappings endpoint provides information about the application's request mappings.
- [Metrics (`metrics`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/metrics.adoc): The metrics endpoint provides access to application metrics to diagnose the metrics the application has recorded.
- [Prometheus (`prometheus`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/prometheus.adoc): The prometheus endpoint provides Spring Boot application's metrics in the format required for scraping by a Prometheus server.
- [Quartz (`quartz`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/quartz.adoc): The quartz endpoint provides information about jobs and triggers that are managed by the Quartz Scheduler.
- [Software Bill of Materials (`sbom`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/sbom.adoc): The sbom endpoint provides information about the software bill of materials (SBOM).
- [Scheduled Tasks (`scheduledtasks`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/scheduledtasks.adoc): The scheduledtasks endpoint provides information about the application's scheduled tasks.
- [Sessions (`sessions`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/sessions.adoc): The sessions endpoint provides information about the application's HTTP sessions that are managed by Spring Session.
- [Shutdown (`shutdown`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/shutdown.adoc): The shutdown endpoint is used to shut down the application.
- [Application Startup (`startup`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/startup.adoc): The startup endpoint provides information about the application's startup sequence.
- [Thread Dump (`threaddump`)](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-actuator-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/api/pages/rest/actuator/threaddump.adoc): The threaddump endpoint provides a thread dump from the application's JVM.

- [Jersey](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/how-to/pages/jersey.adoc): Spring Security can be used to secure a Jersey-based web application in much the same way as it can be used to secure a Spring MVC-based web application.
- [Logging](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/how-to/pages/logging.adoc): Spring Boot has no mandatory logging dependency, except for the Commons Logging API, which is typically provided by Spring Framework's spring-jcl module.

- [Testing GraalVM Native Images](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/how-to/pages/native-image/testing-native-applications.adoc): When writing native image applications, we recommend that you continue to use the JVM whenever possible to develop the majority of your unit and integration tests.

- [Testing](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/how-to/pages/testing.adoc): Spring Boot includes a number of testing utilities and support classes as well as a dedicated starter that provides common test dependencies.
- [Embedded Web Servers](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/how-to/pages/webserver.adoc): Each Spring Boot web application includes an embedded web server.

- [Auditing](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/auditing.adoc): Once Spring Security is in play, Spring Boot Actuator has a flexible audit framework that publishes events (by default, "authentication success", "failure" and "access denied" exceptions).
- [Cloud Foundry Support](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/cloud-foundry.adoc): Spring Boot's spring-boot-cloudfoundry module (part of spring-boot-starter-cloudfoundry) includes additional support that is activated when you deploy to a compatible Cloud Foundry instance.
- [Enabling Production-ready Features](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/enabling.adoc): The {code-spring-boot}/module/spring-boot-actuator[spring-boot-actuator] module provides all of Spring Boot's production-ready features.
- [Endpoints](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/endpoints.adoc): Actuator endpoints let you monitor and interact with your application.
- [Recording HTTP Exchanges](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/http-exchanges.adoc): You can enable recording of HTTP exchanges by providing a bean of type javadoc:org.springframework.boot.actuate.web.exchanges.HttpExchangeRepository[] in your application's configuration.
- [Production-ready Features](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/index.adoc): Spring Boot includes a number of additional features to help you monitor and manage your application when you push it to production.
- [Monitoring and Management over JMX](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/jmx.adoc): Java Management Extensions (JMX) provide a standard mechanism to monitor and manage applications.
- [Loggers](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/loggers.adoc): Spring Boot Actuator includes the ability to view and configure the log levels of your application at runtime.
- [Metrics](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/metrics.adoc): Spring Boot Actuator provides dependency management and auto-configuration for {url-micrometer-site}[Micrometer], an application metrics facade that s…
- [Monitoring and Management Over HTTP](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/monitoring.adoc): If you are developing a web application, Spring Boot Actuator auto-configures all enabled endpoints to be exposed over HTTP.
- [Observability](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/observability.adoc): Observability is the ability to observe the internal state of a running system from the outside.
- [Process Monitoring](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/process-monitoring.adoc): In the spring-boot module, you can find two classes to create files that are often useful for process monitoring:
- [Tracing](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/actuator/tracing.adoc): Spring Boot Actuator provides dependency management and auto-configuration for {url-micrometer-tracing-docs}[Micrometer Tracing], a facade for popular tracer libraries.
- [Data](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/data/index.adoc): Spring Boot integrates with a number of data technologies, both SQL and NoSQL.
- [Working with NoSQL Technologies](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/data/nosql.adoc): Spring Data provides additional projects that help you access a variety of NoSQL technologies, including:
- [SQL Databases](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/data/sql.adoc): The {url-spring-framework-site}[Spring Framework] provides extensive support for working with SQL databases, from direct JDBC access using javadoc:org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient[] or javadoc:org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate[] to complete "object relational mapping" technologies such as Hibernate.
- [Aspect-Oriented Programming](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/aop.adoc): Spring Boot provides auto-configuration for aspect-oriented programming (AOP).
- [Development-time Services](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/dev-services.adoc): Development-time services provide external dependencies needed to run the application while developing it.
- [Creating Your Own Auto-configuration](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/developing-auto-configuration.adoc): If you work in a company that develops shared libraries, or if you work on an open-source or commercial library, you might want to develop your own auto-configuration.
- [Externalized Configuration](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/external-config.adoc): Spring Boot lets you externalize your configuration so that you can work with the same application code in different environments.
- [Core Features](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/index.adoc): This section dives into the details of Spring Boot.
- [Internationalization](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/internationalization.adoc): Spring Boot supports localized messages so that your application can cater to users of different language preferences.
- [JSON](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/json.adoc): Spring Boot provides integration with the following JSON mapping libraries:
- [Kotlin Support](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/kotlin.adoc): Kotlin is a statically-typed language targeting the JVM (and other platforms) which allows writing concise and elegant code while providing {url-kotlin-docs}/java-interop.html[interoperability] with existing libraries written in Java.
- [Logging](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/logging.adoc): Spring Boot uses Commons Logging for all internal logging but leaves the underlying log implementation open.
- [Profiles](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/profiles.adoc): Spring Profiles provide a way to segregate parts of your application configuration and make it be available only in certain environments.
- [SpringApplication](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/spring-application.adoc): The javadoc:org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication[] class provides a convenient way to bootstrap a Spring application that is started from a main() method.
- [SSL](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/ssl.adoc): Spring Boot provides the ability to configure SSL trust material that can be applied to several types of connections in order to support secure communications.
- [Task Execution and Scheduling](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/features/task-execution-and-scheduling.adoc): In the absence of an javadoc:java.util.concurrent.Executor[] bean in the context, Spring Boot auto-configures an javadoc:org.springframework.core.task.AsyncTaskExecutor[].
- [Reference](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/index.adoc): This section provides information on using the features and capabilities of Spring Boot.
- [Caching](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/caching.adoc): The Spring Framework provides support for transparently adding caching to an application.
- [Sending Email](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/email.adoc): The Spring Framework provides an abstraction for sending email by using the javadoc:org.springframework.mail.javamail.JavaMailSender[] interface, and Spring Boot provides auto-configuration for it as well as a starter module.
- [gRPC](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/grpc.adoc): Google Remote Procedure Call (gRPC) is a high-performance RPC framework that enables client-server communication using binary messages.
- [Hazelcast](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/hazelcast.adoc): If Hazelcast is on the classpath and a suitable configuration is found, Spring Boot auto-configures a javadoc:com.hazelcast.core.HazelcastInstance[] that you can inject in your application.
- [IO](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/index.adoc): Most applications will need to deal with input and output concerns at some point.
- [Distributed Transactions With JTA](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/jta.adoc): Spring Boot supports distributed JTA transactions across multiple XA resources by using a transaction manager retrieved from JNDI.
- [Quartz Scheduler](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/quartz.adoc): Spring Boot offers several conveniences for working with the Quartz scheduler, including the spring-boot-starter-quartz starter.
- [Calling REST Services](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/rest-client.adoc): Spring Boot provides various convenient ways to call remote REST services.
- [Spring Batch](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/spring-batch.adoc): Spring Boot offers several conveniences for working with {url-spring-batch-site}[Spring Batch], including running a Job on startup.
- [Validation](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/validation.adoc): The method validation feature supported by Bean Validation 1.1 is automatically enabled as long as a JSR-303 implementation (such as Hibernate validator) is on the classpath.
- [Web Services](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/io/webservices.adoc): Spring Boot provides Web Services auto-configuration so that all you must do is define your javadoc:org.springframework.ws.server.endpoint.annotation.Endpoint[format=annotation] beans.
- [AMQP](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/messaging/amqp.adoc): The Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) is a platform-neutral, wire-level protocol for message-oriented middleware.
- [Messaging](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/messaging/index.adoc): The Spring Framework provides extensive support for integrating with messaging systems, from simplified use of the JMS API using javadoc:org.springframework.jms.core.JmsClient[] to a complete infrastructure to receive messages asynchronously.
- [JMS](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/messaging/jms.adoc): The javadoc:jakarta.jms.ConnectionFactory[] interface provides a standard method of creating a javadoc:jakarta.jms.Connection[] for interacting with a JMS broker.
- [Apache Kafka Support](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/messaging/kafka.adoc): Apache Kafka is supported by providing auto-configuration of the spring-kafka project.
- [Apache Pulsar Support](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/messaging/pulsar.adoc): Apache Pulsar is supported by providing auto-configuration of the {url-spring-pulsar-site}[Spring for Apache Pulsar] project.
- [RSocket](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/messaging/rsocket.adoc): RSocket is a binary protocol for use on byte stream transports.
- [Spring Integration](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/messaging/spring-integration.adoc): Spring Boot offers several conveniences for working with {url-spring-integration-site}[Spring Integration], including the spring-boot-starter-integration starter.
- [WebSockets](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/messaging/websockets.adoc): Spring Boot provides WebSockets auto-configuration for embedded Tomcat and Jetty.
- [AOT Cache](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/aot-cache.adoc): AOT cache is a JVM feature that can help reduce the startup time and memory footprint of Java applications.
- [Ahead-of-Time Processing With the JVM](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/aot.adoc): It's beneficial for the startup time to run your application using the AOT generated initialization code.
- [Checkpoint and Restore With the JVM](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/checkpoint-restore.adoc): Coordinated Restore at Checkpoint (CRaC) is an OpenJDK project that defines a new Java API to allow you to checkpoint and restore an application on the HotSpot JVM.
- [Cloud Native Buildpacks](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/container-images/cloud-native-buildpacks.adoc): Docker images can be built directly from your Maven or Gradle plugin using Cloud Native Buildpacks.
- [Dockerfiles](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/container-images/dockerfiles.adoc): While it is possible to convert a Spring Boot uber jar into a Docker image with just a few lines in the Dockerfile, using the layering feature will result in an optimized image.
- [Efficient Container Images](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/container-images/efficient-images.adoc): It is easily possible to package a Spring Boot uber jar as a Docker image.
- [Container Images](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/container-images/index.adoc): Spring Boot applications can be containerized using Dockerfiles, or by using Cloud Native Buildpacks to create optimized docker compatible container images that you can run anywhere.
- [Efficient Deployments](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/efficient.adoc): You can run your application using the executable jar, but loading the classes from nested jars has a small startup cost.
- [Packaging Spring Boot Applications](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/index.adoc): Spring Boot supports several technologies for optimizing applications for deployment, including GraalVM native images, AOT cache, and Checkpoint and Restore.
- [Advanced Native Images Topics](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/native-image/advanced-topics.adoc): Reflection hints are automatically created for configuration properties by the Spring ahead-of-time engine.
- [GraalVM Native Images](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/native-image/index.adoc): GraalVM Native Images are standalone executables that can be generated by processing compiled Java applications ahead-of-time.
- [Introducing GraalVM Native Images](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/packaging/native-image/introducing-graalvm-native-images.adoc): GraalVM Native Images provide a new way to deploy and run Java applications.
- [Security](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/security/index.adoc): Spring Boot provides helpful support for general purpose security features such as OAuth2 and SAML 2.0.
- [OAuth2](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/security/oauth2.adoc): OAuth2 is a widely used authorization framework.
- [SAML 2.0](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/security/saml2.adoc): SAML v2.0 is a widely adopted framework for exchanging security information between online business partners.
- [Testing](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/testing/index.adoc): Spring Boot provides a number of utilities and annotations to help when testing your application.
- [Testing Spring Applications](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/testing/spring-applications.adoc): One of the major advantages of dependency injection is that it should make your code easier to unit test.
- [Testing Spring Boot Applications](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/testing/spring-boot-applications.adoc): A Spring Boot application is a Spring javadoc:org.springframework.context.ApplicationContext[], so nothing very special has to be done to test it beyond what you would normally do with a vanilla Spring context.
- [Test Modules](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/testing/test-modules.adoc): Spring Boot offers several focused, feature-specific -test modules:
- [Test Scope Dependencies](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/testing/test-scope-dependencies.adoc): The spring-boot-starter-test starter (in the test scope) contains the following provided libraries:
- [Test Utilities](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/testing/test-utilities.adoc): A few test utility classes that are generally useful when testing your application are packaged as part of spring-boot.
- [Testcontainers](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/testing/testcontainers.adoc): The Testcontainers library provides a way to manage services running inside Docker containers.
- [Auto-configuration](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/auto-configuration.adoc): Spring Boot auto-configuration attempts to automatically configure your Spring application based on the jar dependencies that you have added.
- [Build Systems](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/build-systems.adoc): It is strongly recommended that you choose a build system that supports dependency management and that can consume artifacts published to the Maven Central repository.
- [Configuration Classes](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/configuration-classes.adoc): Spring Boot favors Java-based configuration.
- [Developer Tools](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/devtools.adoc): Spring Boot includes an additional set of tools that can make the application development experience a little more pleasant.
- [Developing with Spring Boot](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/index.adoc): This section goes into more detail about how you should use Spring Boot.
- [Packaging Your Application for Production](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/packaging-for-production.adoc): Once your Spring Boot application is ready for production deployment, there are many options for packaging and optimizing the application.
- [Running Your Application](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/running-your-application.adoc): One of the biggest advantages of packaging your application as a jar and using an embedded HTTP server is that you can run your application as you would any other.
- [Spring Beans and Dependency Injection](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/spring-beans-and-dependency-injection.adoc): You are free to use any of the standard Spring Framework techniques to define your beans and their injected dependencies.
- [Structuring Your Code](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/structuring-your-code.adoc): Spring Boot does not require any specific code layout to work.
- [Using the @SpringBootApplication Annotation](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/using/using-the-springbootapplication-annotation.adoc): Many Spring Boot developers like their apps to use auto-configuration, component scan and be able to define extra configuration on their "application class".
- [Graceful Shutdown](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/web/graceful-shutdown.adoc): Graceful shutdown is enabled by default with all three embedded web servers (Jetty, Reactor Netty, and Tomcat) and with both reactive and servlet-based web applications.
- [Web](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/web/index.adoc): Spring Boot is well suited for web application development.
- [Reactive Web Applications](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/web/reactive.adoc): Spring Boot simplifies development of reactive web applications by providing auto-configuration for Spring Webflux.
- [Servlet Web Applications](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/web/servlet.adoc): If you want to build servlet-based web applications, you can take advantage of Spring Boot's auto-configuration for Spring MVC or Jersey.
- [Spring for GraphQL](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/web/spring-graphql.adoc): If you want to build GraphQL applications, you can take advantage of Spring Boot's auto-configuration for {url-spring-graphql-site}[Spring for GraphQL].
- [Spring HATEOAS](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/web/spring-hateoas.adoc): If you develop a RESTful API that makes use of hypermedia, Spring Boot provides auto-configuration for Spring HATEOAS that works well with most applications.
- [Spring Session](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/reference/pages/web/spring-session.adoc): Spring Boot provides {url-spring-session-site}[Spring Session] auto-configuration for a range of data stores.

- [Documentation Overview](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/documentation.adoc): This section provides a brief overview of Spring Boot reference documentation.
- [Spring Boot](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/index.adoc): Spring Boot helps you to create stand-alone, production-grade Spring-based applications that you can run.
- [Installing Spring Boot](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/installing.adoc): Spring Boot can be used with "classic" Java development tools or installed as a command line tool.

- [System Requirements](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/system-requirements.adoc): Spring Boot {version-spring-boot} requires at least Java 17 and is compatible with versions up to and including Java 26.
- [Upgrading Spring Boot](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/upgrading.adoc): Instructions for how to upgrade from earlier versions of Spring Boot are provided on the project {url-github-wiki}[wiki].
- [Nav Root](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/ROOT/partials/nav-root.adoc)

- [Metadata Format](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/configuration-metadata/format.adoc): Configuration metadata files are located inside jars under META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json.

- [Providing Manual Hints](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/configuration-metadata/manual-hints.adoc): To improve the user experience and further assist the user in configuring a given property, you can provide additional metadata that:
- [Alternative Single Jar Solutions](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/executable-jar/alternatives.adoc): If the preceding restrictions mean that you cannot use Spring Boot Loader, consider the following alternatives:
- [The Executable Jar Format](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/executable-jar/index.adoc): The spring-boot-loader modules lets Spring Boot support executable jar and war files.
- [Spring Boot's "`NestedJarFile`" Class](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/executable-jar/jarfile-class.adoc): The core class used to support loading nested jars is javadoc:org.springframework.boot.loader.jar.NestedJarFile[].
- [Launching Executable Jars](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/executable-jar/launching.adoc): The javadoc:org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.Launcher[] class is a special bootstrap class that is used as an executable jar's main entry point.
- [Nested JARs](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/executable-jar/nested-jars.adoc): Java does not provide any standard way to load nested jar files (that is, jar files that are themselves contained within a jar).
- [PropertiesLauncher Features](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/executable-jar/property-launcher.adoc): javadoc:org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.PropertiesLauncher[] has a few special features that can be enabled with external properties (System properties, environment variables, manifest entries, or loader.properties).
- [Executable Jar Restrictions](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/pages/executable-jar/restrictions.adoc): You need to consider the following restrictions when working with a Spring Boot Loader packaged application:
- [Nav Specification](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/specification/partials/nav-specification.adoc)
- [Developing Your First Spring Boot Application](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/tutorial/pages/first-application/index.adoc): This section describes how to develop a small "Hello World!" web application that highlights some of Spring Boot's key features.
- [Tutorials](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/tutorial/pages/index.adoc): This section provides tutorials to help you get started using Spring Boot.
- [Nav Tutorial](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/documentation/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/antora/modules/tutorial/partials/nav-tutorial.adoc)
- [Getting support for Spring Boot](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/SUPPORT.adoc): We choose not to use GitHub issues for general usage questions and support, preferring to use issues solely for the tracking of bugs and enhancements.
